Each measurement describes a different aspect of engine operation, so the component name matters as much as its appearance.

sections.title: Numbered components are not interchangeable labels
sections.body: Several coils and injectors appear together, along with bank-specific camshaft components. The camshaft-position sensor reports shaft position, while variable camshaft timing solenoids control oil flow used to change timing. Finding the correct numbered component prevents information for one cylinder or timing function from being applied to another.

sections.title: Match the illustrated arrangement
sections.body: The 3.7L caption identifies the engine arrangement shown in this complete location view. Use the front-of-vehicle arrow, grid and connector identifiers to orient it. Connector and splice callouts locate reference points; their proximity in the picture does not establish the electrical paths between them.

topics.title: Convertible A-pillar trim
topics.summary: The A-pillar trim covers the interior face of the pillar beside the windshield. This convertible-specific procedure explains how the panel and neighboring sun visor attachments are released, including electrical connections where fitted.

sections.title: Trim finishes the windshield-side structure
sections.body: The trim panel gives the pillar a finished interior surface and covers the area behind it. Clips and retainers hold the panel against its mounting points. Those attachments locate the trim; the decorative panel itself should not be confused with the structural pillar beneath it.

sections.title: The sun visor is part of the access sequence
sections.body: The procedure begins with the sun visor and its cap and clip before releasing the pillar panel. This sequence accounts for the adjoining trim and mounting arrangement. An electrical connector may also be present at the visor, so mechanical release does not always leave that component completely detached.

sections.title: Illustration and equipment notes define the variation
sections.body: The source shows one steering layout and one side, stating that the opposite arrangements are similar. A speaker connector is disconnected only where fitted. These notes explain how to interpret the illustrated example without assuming every convertible has identical electrical equipment behind its A-pillar trim.

topics.title: 3.7L ignition and fuel-pump power distribution
topics.summary: This 3.7L power-distribution sheet shows feeds and switching associated with the six ignition coils and the fuel-pump system. It relates the battery junction box supplies to the fuel-pump relay, body control module and pump controller.

sections.title: Ignition and fuel delivery need electrical energy
sections.body: Coil-on-plug ignition units use electrical energy to produce the spark voltage needed for combustion. The fuel pump system supplies fuel, with a control module participating in pump operation. These are different loads, so a power distribution sheet helps distinguish their supply paths from their detailed operating controls.

sections.title: Supply availability and switching are separate
sections.body: The diagram includes fuses, a fuel pump relay, and a field-effect transistor label at the body control module. It also distinguishes always-live power from power available in start or run. Those annotations describe different supply and switching roles; the illustrated lines establish their actual relationships.

sections.title: Use branch labels and continuation points
sections.body: The 3.7L heading identifies this complete wiring arrangement. Splice and off-page references show where the supplies continue, while component-system references lead to the detailed ignition and fuel-control circuits. Follow each illustrated path separately so the always-live feed and Start-or-Run coil supply retain their different operating conditions.

topics.title: Steering network without adaptive cruise
topics.summary: This sheet shows the high-speed controller area network 2 arrangement without adaptive cruise. It identifies steering-related modules and the head-up display connection within that specific network drawing.

sections.title: Paired wires carry messages
sections.body: Controller area network communication uses a paired data circuit rather than a separate wire for every command. The power steering control module (PSCM), steering column control module (SCCM) and head-up display (HUD) module are named here. Their network connections carry information; they are distinct from the power needed to operate each component.

sections.title: Communication joins otherwise separate functions
sections.body: Power steering uses vehicle information when determining assistance, while steering-column electronics exchange driver-control information. A display also depends on information supplied by other systems. The sheet therefore helps trace a communication concern that may involve several functions, rather than treating each affected feature as an independent failed component.

sections.title: Use the illustrated branch and continuation points
sections.body: The “Without adaptive cruise” heading applies to this complete sheet. Follow both data conductors through its connectors, splices and continuations to understand the illustrated arrangement; the unused connector is a separate local detail. The related network description identifies termination modules whose resistors stabilize signaling, a different function from a power-circuit ground.

topics.title: Adaptive-cruise radar and steering network
topics.summary: This adaptive-cruise network sheet includes the proximity-warning radar, steering controllers and head-up display module on high-speed controller area network 2. It shows the data paths that support communication among those devices.

sections.title: A shared data pair connects controllers
sections.body: The power steering control module (PSCM), steering column control module (SCCM), head-up display (HUD) module and radar unit are named on the sheet. Controller area network communication carries messages over paired conductors. Those conductors transmit information rather than serving as the main power supply for steering assistance or radar operation.

sections.title: Driver assistance depends on shared information
sections.body: Radar supplies information about objects ahead, while the network distributes vehicle information used by participating controllers. A communication concern can affect a function even when its local hardware still has power. The “Adaptive cruise” heading identifies this entire illustrated network configuration, not merely the radar branch.

sections.title: Trace both conductors through the references
sections.body: The positive and negative data labels identify a pair, not ordinary battery-positive and ground connections. Follow both conductors through the drawn splices, connectors and continuation points. The related network chart identifies termination modules, whose resistors stabilize communication; it provides context that cannot be established from neighboring labels alone.

topics.title: 3.7L manual-transmission clutch and speed inputs
topics.summary: This 3.7L manual-transmission sheet shows output-shaft speed sensing and clutch-pedal switches. It distinguishes transmission rotation from the driver’s pedal movement and identifies the controller inputs associated with each.

sections.title: Two different kinds of movement are reported
sections.body: The output shaft speed sensor reports how quickly the transmission's output rotates. Clutch pedal switches report pedal position at particular points in its travel. These are complementary inputs: output rotation describes driveline motion, while pedal state describes the driver's operation of the clutch.

sections.title: Top and bottom switches answer different questions
sections.body: The sheet names top-of-travel and bottom-of-travel clutch pedal position switches, as well as a clutch deactivation label. A pedal can leave its released position long before reaching full depression, so these states should not be treated as interchangeable. The powertrain and body control modules appear as related controllers.

sections.title: Read switch state from its legend
sections.body: The “Manual transmission” heading applies to this complete sheet. Its depressed and released pedal legends establish how to interpret the switch contacts, while connector, ground and off-page references support tracing. The top- and bottom-of-travel switches remain distinct inputs; the sheet does not define every feature that uses them.

topics.title: Door-ajar inputs without memory
topics.summary: This interior-lighting sheet covers the door-ajar arrangement without memory equipment. It relates the front latch switches to the body control module, window regulator motors and their illustrated ground returns.

sections.title: A latch reports door condition
sections.body: A door-ajar switch converts a mechanical door condition into an electrical state. The body control module uses door information when coordinating body functions such as interior lighting. The source explicitly states that these switches are electrically closed when the door is closed, an important distinction from everyday uses of 'open.'

sections.title: Door information crosses system boundaries
sections.body: The sheet names both front latch assemblies and both front window regulator motors, with references into their system diagrams. Door-status information therefore matters beyond a lamp alone. The “Without memory” heading applies to this complete arrangement; its illustrated ground returns should not be substituted for the module-return arrangement on the memory sheet.

sections.title: Trace the illustrated return paths
sections.body: Ground references, splice identifiers, and body controller door-ajar labels help organize the circuit. Their exact relationships come from the drawn lines, not the order of extracted text. The latch's release motor and its door-status switch are different functions even when they appear within the same named assembly.

topics.title: Door-ajar inputs with memory
topics.summary: This memory-equipment sheet shows how the front door-ajar switches report door condition. It includes return connections at the driver and passenger door modules rather than the ground-return arrangement shown on the without-memory sheet.

sections.title: A mechanical latch creates an electrical state
sections.body: The door-ajar switches change electrical state with door condition, providing information used by the body control module. The source explicitly says the switches are closed when the doors are closed. Here, an electrically closed switch means a conducting contact, which is distinct from whether a lamp is illuminated.

sections.title: Return labels distinguish this arrangement
sections.body: The diagram names return connections at the driver and passenger door modules alongside the latch switches and window regulator circuits. Those returns provide the intended electrical references for the status signals. The “Memory” heading applies to this whole arrangement; its connections should be matched to the vehicle’s equipment.

sections.title: Follow status information across the references
sections.body: The body controller's left-front and right-front door-ajar labels identify the information being reported. References to latch and window diagrams provide further context for the named assemblies. Use the illustrated wiring to establish how the returns and signals connect; proximity in the extracted text does not establish a shared path.

topics.title: Rear lamp power and monitoring: China and Europe
topics.summary: This China-and-Europe rear-lamp sheet separates position, stop and turn functions in the lamp assemblies. It also shows lamp-outage information and related body-control connections for that market arrangement.

sections.title: One assembly performs several visible jobs
sections.body: Position lamps make the vehicle visible, stop lamps communicate braking, and turn lamps indicate a change of direction. The assignments distinguish these functions and their ground connections. Because the assembly contains separate electrical functions, seeing one light operate does not establish that every other path into the housing is working.

sections.title: Switching and monitoring appear together
sections.body: The body control module (BCM) outputs include field-effect transistor (FET) labels, identifying electronic switching devices. Body Control Module B and outage labels also appear. Outage-related circuits concern lamp monitoring, so their purpose differs from the current paths that illuminate the lamps; the drawn schematic establishes their exact relationship.

sections.title: Use the market labels at their branches
sections.body: The “China, Europe” heading applies to this entire rear-lamp arrangement. Follow its left and right assembly references, grounds and turn/stop/hazard continuations without substituting another market’s layout. Always-live supply annotations describe availability; the control electronics determine whether each connected lamp function illuminates.

topics.title: Convertible rear power-window control
topics.summary: This convertible rear-window sheet shows the left and right motor assemblies, their operating supplies and their control inputs. It also identifies the accessory-delay circuit and body-control connections that support window operation.

sections.title: Motor energy and movement requests are distinct
sections.body: The motor assemblies have battery supply and ground labels alongside up, down, ajar, and global-down labels. Power provides the energy to move the glass, while control inputs determine requested behavior. The presence of battery voltage alone therefore does not establish that a movement request has reached a motor.

sections.title: The sheet includes permission to operate
sections.body: The body control module and a non-serviceable accessory delay relay appear with delayed-accessory connections. This identifies an operating-power or enable context beyond the direction commands. Body Control Module B also appears with down-related labels; the illustrated lines establish its exact relationship to the rear-window control paths.

sections.title: Follow the matching equipment branch
sections.body: The “Convertible” heading applies to the complete rear-window drawing. Off-page power-window references continue the control paths, while fuse and ground references identify the supplies and returns. The schematic describes electrical connections rather than the physical wire route through the rear body, and it should not be applied as a coupe window arrangement.

topics.title: Memory-equipped driver mirror motors and feedback
topics.summary: This memory-equipped driver-mirror sheet identifies adjustment motors, position feedback, heating and lighting around the driver door module and left exterior mirror. The whole drawing applies to that memory arrangement.

sections.title: Movement and position are separate signals
sections.body: Small motors tilt the mirror horizontally and vertically, changing the rearward view. Position potentiometers are variable electrical elements that report mirror position. Their feed, return, and signal paths let a controller distinguish where the mirror is from the command that tells a motor to move.

sections.title: Several features share the mirror assembly
sections.body: The driver door module connects to heating, a turn indicator and puddle lighting as well as the adjustment circuits. Heating clears moisture through electrical heat, while the lamps provide signaling or nearby illumination. The “Memory” heading qualifies this complete arrangement, including the position-feedback circuits that distinguish it from simpler mirror systems.

sections.title: Use the function labels to follow each path
sections.body: Motor direction labels describe movement commands, while potentiometer labels describe position feedback. Ground and interior-lamp references provide additional tracing points. Treat these as separate functions within a shared assembly, and use the drawn connections to establish relationships instead of assuming that adjacent extracted labels share a circuit.

connector-C226A.summary: The steering column mechanically connects the steering wheel to the steering gear; C226A belongs to the nearby steering column control module, which interfaces with the wheel and column switches. This 12-cavity view maps its supply, ground, communication and feature-specific circuits, including the applicable SelectShift paddle connections.

G1726383.summary: See how the steering column, upper shaft, lower shaft and coupling form the mechanical connection from the steering wheel to the steering gear. The lower shaft is collapsible, and the source requires a measurement whenever it is disconnected from the upper shaft or coupling.

G1693270.summary: This procedure removes and refits the SCCM assembly and its electrical connections. If a new module is being installed, its scan-tool configuration process begins with the old SCCM still connected and is completed after the replacement is fitted.

G1702174.summary: This procedure replaces the electronic column lock, including access, its special retaining fasteners and the configuration work required for a new module. The BCM configuration and training steps are part of making the replacement lock operate correctly.

connector-C2434.summary: C2434 is the steering column lock module’s four-cavity connector. Its view identifies an unused position and separate supply, ground and LIN circuits, helping you distinguish the lock wiring from the SCCM connector beside the steering wheel.

G1693265.summary: This overview connects the steering-column stalks, steering-wheel buttons and applicable paddle switches with the functions they control. It also introduces the push-button ignition and column-lock systems, whose modules and connectors have different roles.

G1693266.summary: This reference explains how push-button ignition and the electronic column lock interact with the BCM, vehicle networks and start authorization. Use its system diagrams and operating conditions to understand the lock’s power, communication and configuration requirements.

wiring-081-003.summary: This diagram traces the SCCM’s LIN and separate high-speed-wiper circuits to the windshield-wiper motor, then shows the motor’s related washer and ground connections. Its rain-sensitive branch is identified separately, so follow the equipment-specific path.

wiring-030-003.summary: This 6R80 diagram follows the upshift, downshift and signal-return circuits through the SCCM connection and clockspring to the steering-wheel paddle switches. It describes the automatic-transmission paddle arrangement rather than every Mustang steering wheel.

wiring-112-003.summary: This Security Pack wiring diagram shows the column lock’s supply relay, BCM control and monitoring, LIN communication and ground path. Match it to the vehicle’s equipment before using its connector and circuit references.
